kits.description: The Cisco NXK-ACC-KIT-1RU rack-mount kit for 1 RU Nexus fixed switches. It holds two front brackets, two rear brackets and two slider rails, with a ground lug kit and screws. The brackets screw to the switch side and the rails to the rear posts of a four-post rack. The switch slides onto the rails.

The Cisco NXK-ACC-KIT2-2RU rack-mount kit. It holds two inner rails that screw to the chassis side, two outer rails that latch to the front and rear posts, and flat-head screws. The chassis slides onto the outer rails.

gaps.note: The guide's appendix D, Additional Kits (page 59 to 60, PDF page 65 to 66), has no content. The NXK-ACC-KIT-1RU parts are read from the rack-mount procedure (page 20) alone: front brackets, rear brackets and slider rails, with countersink screws and no ground lug kit.
gaps.wanted: The NXK-ACC-KIT-1RU contents table for this switch, as the FX3 and FX3S guides print it. The parts carried agree with those guides.

gaps.note: The guide's installation options list "Rack-mount kit (N3K-C3064-ACC-KIT) which you can order from Cisco" and say nothing else of it: no contents, no figure, no procedure, no depth range.
gaps.wanted: The kit's contents and its rack depth range, from a document that describes it. It is not listed under the kits of this device, because a kit needs parts and a range.

A drawing of the lid, the underside and the two side walls. The guide's overview shows one side wall in three-quarter view and calls out its mounting-bracket screw holes and a grounding pad; none is flat and none can be measured. Each face carries an `empty:` sentence.

gaps.note: The guide's weights table gives 2.42 lb (1.1 kg) against the 500 W AC supply and has no row for the 1200 W HVAC/HVDC or the 930 W DC supply. No weight is carried for either.
gaps.wanted: The weight of the N9K-PUV-1200W and the NXA-PDC-930W, from a document that prints it.

A picture of the 930 W DC and the 1200 W HVAC/HVDC supply. The guide's figure shows AC supplies only, and its replacement chapter has no picture. Their faces are the AC supply's with the inlet changed.
A stated size for the supply and the fan module. The guide gives "Form factor RSP1" for every supply and nothing for the fan.

A cage skin with a bail. The guide's rear figure draws the management SFP port with a latch plate across the foot of its opening; the library's SFP cage has one skin and none shows a bail, and a second skin on it would move every device that seats it.

gaps.note: The Overview says the switch "will power down due to a fan-policy trigger if fewer than 3 fans are operational" and, in another note, that it "runs with +1 redundancy mode".
gaps.wanted: Whether the first sentence counts fan modules or rotors. It is read as modules, three of four, so the group says 3+1.

a `power-draw-max-w` on each module this chassis accepts, from the vendor's own per-card table - Cisco publishes one per ambient, most vendors publish none, and until they land a module total is a floor

chassis-lamps.note: Callout 3 is "BCN, STS, ENV LEDs"; appendix C says they sit "on the left side of the front". The figure draws three lamps in a row under the first jacks, each with its legend to its left, at 20.2, 29.5 and 39.3 mm across and 39.4 mm down. The vertical is measured from the figure's top and bottom edges, 127 px for 43.7 mm, 2.9 px per mm. The lamps are flat rectangles, about twice as wide as high, so they are common/led-rect-sm@1 (2.8 x 1.6), the part the rear's lamps use, centred on those points, and not the square lamp; the lamp rows and the legend sit 4.3 mm above the bottom edge. The legend after them reads CISCO NEXUS N9K-C93108TC-FX3, from 41.8 mm; the library's practice for a Cisco face is that text, as on the 93180YC-EX, and no logo artwork. The figure's mark at the top left is not drawn. Under the jacks the figure draws two rows of small cells: an upper row from 75.2 mm to the right end, beside the legend, and a lower row that runs the whole width from 18.3 to 421.5 mm.

colour.note: NO SOURCE FOR THE COLOUR. The guide's figures are uncoloured line art. #d0d2cf is the value the 93180YC-EX's stencil sample gave, carried across as a family colour; it is a relative's figure and not a reading of this device.

gate-1.note: The front figure's body, between its two fold lines, is 1254 px across and 126 px down: aspect 9.96 against the guide's 17.3 x 1.72 in, 10.05, so 0.9% out, and it can be measured; 2.854 px per mm across from 439.4 mm and 2.883 down from 43.7. The rear figure's body is 1248 px across and 126 down, 9.90, 1.5% out, 2.840 px per mm across. A repeated feature checks the scale: the jack columns step 40.25 px, 14.10 mm, against the registry's 13.97 (0.9% out, the same as the aspect), so every pitch is the registry's and the figure fixes where each group starts.

interface-names.note: mgmt0 is stated: the guide's setup chapter asks for "the Management (Mgmt0) interface". Ethernet1/1 to Ethernet1/54 are NOT IN THE GUIDE (searched for "Ethernet1/": none) and the NetBox device-type file, which names them, is not held, only its path. They are the slot/port form NX-OS uses on the fixed Nexus 9300 and are not written into the device: the faceplate prints 1 to 54.

port-lamps.note: Appendix C, Switch Chassis LEDs: "The port LEDs appear as triangles pointing up or down to the nearest port." Green is admin up, module present and link up; amber is admin down or module absent; off is up and present but no link. The figure draws an up triangle at the left and a down triangle at the right of each column's upper jack, and one at each end of each QSFP28 band with four small windows between them. The windows are drawn as marks and carry no state; the guide does not name them.

port-order.note: The figure prints a pair of numerals over each column, "1 up down 2" to "47 up down 48", and "49 up down 50", "51 ..." and "53 ..." over the QSFP28 pairs, so the odd port is the upper cage or jack. The guide's text gives the ports as 1-48 and 49-54. Port numbers are as printed; the NX-OS interface names are in the interface-names entry.

power.note: Appendix B, Switch Power Input Requirements: typical 420 W and maximum 464 W "(AC or DC)", 1583 BTU per hour. The figures are the switch's draw and not a supply rating; the guide names no configuration or ambient.

rack-ears.note: The guide's NXK-ACC-KIT-1RU procedure draws the front bracket screwed to the chassis side in a figure shared with the 93180YC-FX3 guide, and says the holes used depend on the rack and on the clearance needed for interface cables, 3 inches minimum, and for module handles, 1 inch minimum. The NXK-ACC-KIT2-2RU procedure says the chassis slides onto the rails "until the front panel is flush with the front of the rack". No figure dimensions a position and none says which the box ships with, so the two positions are written without an `at`, named for what the text says they clear, and none is the default.

rear-face.note: Every x and y on the power-supply side is read off the rear figure (2.840 px per mm across, 2.883 down). Supply 1, four fan modules, then the console jack over the RJ-45 management jack, the SFP management port, the USB port stood on end, and supply 2. THE OUT-OF-BAND BLOCK SITS BETWEEN THE FANS AND SUPPLY 2, not beyond supply 2 as on the 93180YC-EX. Two lamps with a screw between them stand under the jacks, with the legends BCN and STS, which the figure prints. The fan handles were redrawn from a 5x enlargement of fan 1 (grey pads, a squeeze bar at each side of the hub, grip marks on the left). The figure draws the management SFP cage with a latch plate across the foot of its opening; the library's std/sfp@1 has one skin and no cage with a bail, so the cage is the plain one. A bail skin on std/sfp@1 would rehash 121 devices.

sources.note: One guide, held as PDF and as converted text and figures; it is not committed. Cisco N93108TC-FX3 NX-OS Mode Switch Hardware Installation Guide, First Published 2023-12-14, Last Modified 2026-07-16, 66 pages: the overview and its figures (art numbers 505474 and 505475, and a three-quarter view), appendix B specifications, appendix C LEDs, the rack-mounting chapter. NO DATA SHEET, PHOTOGRAPH, 3D MODEL OR STENCIL IS HELD for this model, and the NetBox devicetype-library is held as a path listing only: it names a device type and a front and a rear elevation for this model, and neither file was read. THE GUIDE'S FIGURES ARE FLAT LINE ART AND CARRY CALLOUTS: the front is 1254 px across the body at this size, 2.85 px per mm, so every position here is a reading good to about a millimetre. The 93180YC-FX3 and 93180YC-FX3S guides were read for the supplies and kits they share with this one.

stack-orientation.note: The library's convention: the upper cage upright over the lower turned 180, and the upper jack turned 180 over the lower one. The front figure draws the upper jacks with their latch notch up and a lamp triangle in each top corner, and the lower jacks with the notch down, which is that arrangement. The three QSFP28 pairs follow the same rule.

the-width.note: The guide's Switch Dimensions table: "17.3 inches (43.9 cm)" wide, "17.9 inches (45.7 cm)" deep and "1.72 inches (4.4 cm) (1 RU)" high; the weights table gives the chassis "15.8 lb (7.1 kg)". 439.4 mm, 454.7 mm and 43.7 mm are carried, the inch figures converted. The metric weight is carried as printed; 15.8 lb is 7.17 kg.

the-x-axis.note: From the front figure at 2.854 px per mm, origin the left fold line. Three groups of eight jack columns start at 9.3, 130.5 and 251.7 mm, a stride of 121.2: at the registry's 13.97 mm pitch that is a gutter of 9.4 mm. The figure shows the same gap, 28 px, between the groups. The three QSFP28 cages start at 368.3, 390.6 and 412.9 mm: the figure's step is 63.6 px, 22.3 mm, and its right edge, 433.1, fits 20 mm cages. The 93180YC-EX steps its QSFP28 cages 24.4 mm and this figure does not.

the-y-axis.note: From the same figure, origin the top fold line. The upper jacks run 10.4 to 20.6 mm and the lower jacks 26.0 to 36.0, and the QSFP28 block 10.7 to 36.3; two jack cells of the registry's 11.0 fill 10.4 to 37.0 on a 15.6 row pitch, which is the pitch used for the jacks; the 10.15 high QSFP28 cages use 15.4. THE LAMP TRIANGLES AND THE NUMERALS ARE DRAWN HIGHER THAN THE FIGURE SHOWS THEM. The figure puts each lamp in a top corner of the upper jack, beside its latch slot; the library's jack cell is a plain rectangle, and a lamp placed over it is an overlap error (L13, L39). So the lamps sit in a row just above the cells, 2.5 mm higher than the figure's, and the numerals and arrows above them move up by the same amount. Their x is the figure's.
